status: C++ WRITTEN AND COMPILED; the authored content is the editor pass
vision: Water is what makes this game sing. Rain droplets disperse over the horizon when the beat hits; the Chladni figure and the FluidNinja dispersion share one field; the puddles sing with the bass; bubbles dot the skyline; Melusina's hair globulates and her movement leaves a trail. Surreal, reverent, grieving - the identity canon, with water as the instrument.
owner_decision_2026_10_22: The owner asked for spectacle beyond the literal Jev pick (a covered hard cut). Jev's STRUCTURE is kept - a held beat, a covered middle, an aftermath that carries the weight - and the spectacle is built under it. Owner's word is canon.

what_the_cpp_does_now.why_a_plain_class: It adds no reflected surface, so it needs no UHT pass and it owns no new authority on an existing surface. It READS the palette; it writes nothing.

the_fluid_binding.mechanism: The world's FluidNinja Live Actors are found by class name and their exposed user parameters are bound BY ROLE (density, strength, beat, input, colour), not by hard-coded names. A renamed upstream parameter becomes a log line, not a silent no-op.
the_fluid_binding.the_singing_puddles: The bass band from MPC_Melodia_Palette drives the bound strength: the water moves with the music instead of near it. READ ONLY.

the_editor_pass_tomorrow.why: The authored content cannot be built offline: placing the FluidNinja Live Actors, choosing the presets, the bone tracking and the output materials are editor work. The C++ is ready to drive it the moment it exists.
steps: place a FluidNinja Live Actor (BP_NinjaLive) for the Poitou canal and one per puddle area; give it the MI_FVOL/MI_HVOL output materials it needs
set the Live Component's user parameters so the ROLE names the C++ binds to exist (density / strength / beat / input / colour), or rename the C++ roles in one place (Tools/waveharp/increments/)
enable the bone reader on the character Live Actor and add Melusina's hair bones - that is what beads her hair
verify: the log must print MELODIA_WATER_CHORUS bound for each surface with the roles it found; a missing role is a one-line fix, not a mystery

transparency_check.finding: the project sets NO explicit translucency or OIT options in Config/DefaultEngine.ini, so the water, the bubbles and the globules inherit the engine defaults - and they are exactly the case the reference studio had to solve: many small overlapping translucent sprites that sort wrongly.
transparency_check.reference: Infinity Nikki redeveloped order-independent transparency for their sheer fabrics; the same sorting problem appears in a field of bubbles.
transparency_check.what_to_do: check the sorting of the overlapping bubbles and globules in the editor pass; the project already owns MF_CustomTranslucency for translucent surfaces. A lookdev decision with a measured answer belongs to the editor pass, not to the night.
